name: Martin Krutský
affiliation: Intelligent Data Analysis Lab, FEE, Czech Technical University in Prague
tagline: Responsible AI · Mechanistic interpretability · Neurosymbolic AI
about: I am a PhD student at the Intelligent Data Analysis Lab, Faculty of Electrical Engineering at the Czech Technical University in Prague, supervised by Gustav Šír. I work on making AI systems understandable and accountable: mechanistic interpretability to understand what models actually compute, and responsible AI to make sure explanations serve oversight, regulation, and the people affected by AI decisions.

I co-founded Responsible AI in Prague, an initiative organizing talks, debates, and the Prague Workshop on Responsible AI. Our research assesses explainability methods for AI governance; we derived XAI desiderata from the EU AI Act. I am a member of the CTU Ethics Committee and an ethics reviewer for NeurIPS.

On the technical side, my PhD develops neurosymbolic methods for mechanistic interpretability, such as logic-guided circuit discovery and provably sufficient explanations of graph neural networks. This autumn, I am an Applied Research Intern at Superhuman (formerly Grammarly), using natural language autoencoders to explain AI-text detectors and AI humanizer models. I took part in the EleutherAI Summer of Open AI Research (SOAR), studying sparse autoencoder pathologies that mimic feature hierarchy. Before and alongside research, I spent 5+ years in industry ML engineering, from NLP models to shipped LLM applications.
